thesis: Ivory Tower rewards a full hand with free life every upkeep, allowing slow decks to turn card conservation into a buffer against aggression.

canonicalIdentity.originalPrintedText: At the beginning of your upkeep, you gain X life, where X is the number of cards in your hand minus 4.

competitiveTimeline.significance: Ivory Tower became a hallmark of early control and a mirror image of Black Vise, linking hand size to life totals in some of the game’s first resource-engine decks.

playbook.role: Preserve cards when the life matters, combine the Tower with draw engines, and avoid spending resources merely to maximize the trigger if doing so weakens board control.
